Reviewing the plan against the feature scope and inspecting cited codebase paths.
schema_version	scope	severity	focus_area	location	what	scenario_or_breakage	suggested_fix
1	in_scope	important	correctness	skills/design/scripts/design-clarify.sh:189-205	The thin wrapper pause-save path only sources session env for REPO; it does not load `.design-step0-route-state.env` first. Current bash loads route-state REPO before the pause check and passes `${REPO:+--repo "$REPO"}` to pause-save. When REPO exists only in the route sidecar, pause-save runs without explicit repo context and may target the wrong issue or fail repo resolution. Before the `.pause-requested` exec, mirror bash: load allowlisted REPO from `.design-step0-route-state.env` when session env lacks it, then forward `--repo` to pause-save when set.
1	in_scope	important	correctness	python/clarify.py:45-72	Publish-phase route-state read failure is not specified. Current bash writes `CLARIFY_PUBLISH_STATUS=route-state-read-failed` and exits without `stage_failed_clarify`; fetch-phase failures stage terminal state. The plan groups route-state failures under fetch staging only. A single staging rule would change publish failure semantics and SUMMARY_OUTCOME handling on publish entry. Document and implement phase-specific branches: fetch route-state failure stages failed-clarify; publish route-state failure emits `CLARIFY_PUBLISH_STATUS=route-state-read-failed` with no staging, matching today's bash.
1	in_scope	important	completeness	python/clarify.py:90-94	The plan omits the operator-visible stdout warning when `SESSION_ID` is empty. Current bash prints `**⚠ /design: SESSION_ID missing; skipping design log publish**` before continuing with response post and label removal; the existing shell harness asserts this string. Dropping it removes a user-visible parity signal during clarify publish. Preserve the same warning on stdout when skipping log publish due to empty `SESSION_ID`.
1	in_scope	important	risk-integration	python/clarify.py:79-81	[SCOPE-REDUCTION] The plan adds a fail-closed truncation-sentinel check on redacted plan output; current bash only rejects empty redacted files and would still write a truncated plan. This expands behavior beyond G6.1 parity and leaves the publish status token unspecified for truncation. Drop the truncation-sentinel gate to match bash parity, or if kept, define the exact `CLARIFY_PUBLISH_STATUS`/`SUMMARY_OUTCOME` pair and add an explicit parity test.
1	out_of_scope	latent	architecture	python/clarify.py:26-27	The plan introduces a new `_read_result_env` helper instead of reusing `design_lifecycle.phase_driver_read_result_env`, which already enforces the same allowlist and symlink refusal contract. Duplication increases maintenance cost without changing wire behavior. Consider reusing `phase_driver_read_result_env` in a follow-up cleanup issue.
